prompt:
You are analyzing **one block of a longer dialogue** to extract actions.

**ACTION** = An atomic communicative act a speaker **directly performed** in a turn.
- Atomic action = minimal unit of action the speaker directly performed. - e.g.
"User asks to find a paper about HCI in NLP conferences" → split into "User asks
to find a paper about HCI", "User asks to find a paper in NLP conferences".
- Include evidence quote from the utterance.

**Possible action types** (generate new types if needed):
Accept, Acknowledge, Address, Allow, Analyze, Apologize, Ask, Challenge, Clarify,
Classify, Compare, Complain, Confirm, Connect, Constrain, Critique, Decide, Define,
Delegate, Describe, Draft, Emphasize, Evaluate, Explain, Feedback, Formalize, Frame,
Greet, Hypothesize, Implement, Include, Infer, Instruct, Invite, Justify, List,
Modify, Observe, Plan, Provide, Qualify, Recommend, Refuse, Report, Request, State,
Suggest, Summarize, Warn

**Role:** **SHAPER | EXECUTOR | OTHER**
* **SHAPER:** Creates/shapes/revises the goal/requirement by proposing new ideas,
new tasks, constraints, alternatives, or directions.
* **EXECUTOR:** Executes/achieves the desired outcome/goal/requirement (e.g.,
drafting text, providing requested information, coding, searching, implementing).
* **OTHER:** Neither SHAPER nor EXECUTOR.

**Turn ID format:** each turn is labeled **U(x,y)** or **A(x,y)**, where **U**=user
turn, **A**=AI turn, **x**=the pair number this turn belongs to (the 1st user+AI
exchange is pair 1, the 2nd is pair 2, etc.), and **y**=the action's position
within that turn (1, 2, 3… in the order it was extracted). e.g. the user's 2nd
atomic action in pair 1 is "U(1,2)"; the AI's 1st atomic action in pair 3 is
"A(3,1)". Use this format for every turn id below — do not use plain integers.

Now I'm preparing the AntiGravity brief for him—he wants a detailed, outcome-focused prompt that scans his portfolio site repo and extracts key information, keeping it short and actionable per his preferences. I need to structure this as a paste-ready brief with a testing checklist at the end. I'm thinking through the scope carefully — the agent will need to handle CSS files, inline styles in JSX, and hardcoded color values scattered through JavaScript and shader code, since that's where design drift tends to hide. I should give him clear guidance on the near-miss threshold so he knows when something counts as a drift versus an exact match, and keep the brief outcome-focused without prescribing the parsing mechanism. Done

Here's Step 1.

This runs in 🟢 AntiGravity. Open your repo there and paste the brief below verbatim. It's deliberately short and outcome-shaped — it tells the agent what artifact to produce and the hard rules, and lets it pick how to parse. One thing to set first: confirm the repo path in the brief matches yours (memory has ~/Documents/jayon-portfolio/site/ — fix it if it's moved).

📋 AntiGravity brief — paste this

TASK: Audit design-token drift across the site. READ-ONLY. Do not modify any source file. Produce one report file.

CANONICAL YARDSTICK:
src/styles/colors_and_type.css (find the actual path) is the single source of truth.
It defines all design tokens as CSS custom properties: colors (--neutral-*, --chroma-*),
type scale (--text-*), font families (--font-*), tracking/leading, spacing (--space-*),
radius (--radius-*), and motion (--dur-*, --ease-*). Parse it first and hold the full token table.

GOAL:
Walk every page and component in the live app (routes: box, brain, creative, technology, about —
their page files plus the components they render). For each APPLIED visual value you find,
decide whether it traces back to a token. "Applied value" = any concrete color, font-size,
font-family, font-weight, letter-spacing, line-height, margin/padding/gap, border-radius,
transition-duration, or easing — wherever it lives: CSS, inline JSX style props, hardcoded
hex/rgb/px/rem in JS/JSX, and hardcoded color values inside GLSL shader strings or Three.js
material definitions.

CLASSIFY each applied value into one of three buckets:
- EXACT       — uses var(--token) OR a literal that equals a token's value exactly.
- NEAR-MISS   — a literal that is CLOSE to a token but not equal. (Colors: within ~10 per RGB
                channel of a token. Sizes/spacing: numerically within ~15% of a token's value.)
                These are the dangerous ones — they look intentional but bypass the system.
- ORPHAN      — a hardcoded literal with no token cousin at all.
Skip EXACT values that already use var(--…); only list literals (EXACT-literal, NEAR-MISS, ORPHAN).

OUTPUT — write a single file: design-audit-raw.md
- One section per page/route, in route order.
- Inside each section, a markdown table with columns:
  | File:Line | Property | Raw value | Nearest token | Bucket |
- After all sections, a SUMMARY block:
  - count of NEAR-MISS and ORPHAN per category (color / type / spacing / radius / motion)
  - the 10 most-repeated offending literals (value + occurrence count) — these are the
    highest-leverage fixes.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Read-only. Touch nothing but the new report file.
- If a value is genuinely ambiguous, list it and tag the bucket with a "?".
- Do not propose fixes or rewrite tokens. Inventory only. I reconcile separately.

Why it's built this way (teaching)

The whole audit hinges on the near-miss bucket. An orphan (some random #777) is obvious and harmless to spot. The corrosive drift is the value that's almost a token — #E5503C sitting where --chroma-red #E34C3B belongs. It renders nearly identically, so it never gets caught by eye, but it means that color can never be changed system-wide from one place. The "10 most-repeated offenders" summary is the payoff: it turns a long inventory into a short fix-list ranked by leverage.

✅ Testing checklist

design-audit-raw.md exists at repo root and opens cleanly.

Every live route has its own section (box, brain, creative, technology, about) — none silently skipped.

Each table row has all five columns filled, with a real File:Line you could click to.

At least the color and type categories have entries (a site this expressive will have some drift — an all-empty report means the scan missed inline/JSX/shader values; re-run if so).

The SUMMARY block has per-category counts and a top-10 repeated-offenders list.

No source file other than the report was modified (check git status — only one new untracked file).

When it's done, drop design-audit-raw.md into this chat and reply "Finish Step" — Step 3 (the reconciliation + verdict) happens here, after Step 2's visual capture. Stuck or the output looks thin? Stay here and tell me what you got.
=== DIALOGUE BLOCK END ===

Now, extract ALL actions from EVERY turn. Return JSON only, pretty-printed with

"action text": "<brief description in third person>", "role":
"<SHAPER|EXECUTOR|OTHER>", "evidence quote": "<quote from utterance>" } ]
}
Respond with ONLY the JSON object. No additional text.
